Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifications and requirements from our security/compliance side before we schedule a call: 

1) Telemetry vendors: we need to know whether request-level identifiers (request_id, user_id, input text) are ever shared with any telemetry or analytics partner. If yes, under what controls and for how long?

2) Logging vs. retention: Our legal team will not accept raw customer input stored beyond 30 days for EU residents. For US traffic we are flexible but want the option to limit retention to 90 days. Can Redwood support per-customer retention windows (i.e., Acme-configured retention policy)?

3) Marketplace/Cloud flow: If we route traffic via Google Marketplace / Azure Marketplace deploys, do the cloud provider contracts introduce new subprocessors (e.g., telemetry or billing partners)? We need a mapping of which subprocessors are active in hosted vs. marketplace flows.

4) SOC2 & procurement: please send SOC2 Type 2 summary and the subprocessors CSV (we'll feed into our vendor portal). Also any references for encryption-in-transit / at-rest details would be useful.

Happy to review the docs you attach.

Hi Alice —

Thanks — great questions. Looping in Neha (Head of Trust & Safety Partnerships) and Dev (solutions infra) so they can answer in detail. High-level answers below while Neha/Dev confirm specifics: 

- Telemetry: Our default hosted API streams anonymized telemetry (aggregated latencies, error rates, pseudonymized request IDs) to our observability partners. We do not send raw input text or unredacted user_ids off-platform by default. We can support configurations to redact or avoid sending request-level identifiers to partners for customers that require it.

- Retention: Redwood supports per-customer retention policies on hosted accounts. You can specify EU vs US retention windows; we can set EU to 30d and US to 90d as an initial config. For Dedicated/Private deployments, retention is fully customer-controlled.

- Marketplace/Cloud: Marketplace deployments may involve cloud marketplace billing and telemetry flows; in those cases the cloud provider may appear as a subprocessor for billing/usage metering. We will provide a matrix showing which subprocessors are active per deployment mode (hosted, dedicated, marketplace).

Neha / Dev: can you confirm the telemetry partner list (and whether any partners receive request-level fields by default), plus the SOC2 excerpt we can share with Acme?

Thanks —
Marissa

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Marissa — joining in with the technical detail you asked for. Answers below are what we provide to customers during security reviews; I'll attach the SOC2 excerpt and the canonical subprocessors CSV.

1) Telemetry / Observability vendors:
   - Default partners: Honeycomb (app-level traces), Prometheus + Grafana Cloud (metrics), SumoLogic (aggregate logs for platform ops).
   - Data shared: by default we push metrics (counts, histograms) and traces with pseudonymized request_ids. We do NOT forward full request payloads or raw input text to third-party telemetry systems in hosted mode.
   - Configurations: for customers that require stricter controls we offer two options: (a) redact request identifiers before shipping to telemetry partners; or (b) disable telemetry forwarding completely and provide self-hosted collectors in a Dedicated/Private deployment. Both can be set at account level.

2) Request-level logging and retention:
   - Hosted: per-account retention policy available; typical presets: 30d, 90d, 180d. We can set EU accounts to 30d by default.
   - Logs you (Acme) asked for (access/audit logs): we retain audit logs for 180 days and can stream them to your SIEM if requested under an approved data transfer addendum.

3) Marketplace / Cloud provider subprocessors:
   - Marketplace flows (GCP/Azure marketplace) will list the cloud provider as an infrastructure subprocessor and the marketplace billing integrator as a billing subprocessor. No additional telemetry partners are automatically added in marketplace flow; telemetry sharing policy remains per-account.

4) Attachments: attaching the canonical subprocessors CSV (includes vendor name, purpose, data processed, region) and a SOC2 Type II excerpt showing controls for logging, encryption, and change management.
